terms.gloss: in vain, to no purpose, for nothing
evidence: Plaut. Aul. 178: Praesāgībat mī animus frūstrā mē īre, quom exībam domō
Cic. de Or. 2.144: frūstrā implōrārī (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: In early Latin also “in error”: frūstrā esse, to be mistaken.

evidence: Plaut. Asin. 698: nē istuc nēquīquam dīxerīs
Caes. BC 1.1: nēquīquam alicujus auxilium implōrāre (Lewis & Short)

phrases.latin: Praesāgībat mī animus frūstrā mē īre, quom exībam domō.
phrases.english: I had a feeling, when I left the house, that I was going for nothing.

sources: Lewis & Short: frustra · Lewis & Short: nequiquam
